fmt::format End-to-End Flow

Complete trace of what happens when you call fmt::format("{}", x)

High-Level Overview

fmt::format("{}", x) ↓ make_format_args(x) → type-erased arguments ↓ vformat() → creates buffer ↓ vformat_to() → parses format string & visits args ↓ formatter specializations → writes each arg ↓ to_string(buffer) → returns std::string

Step 1: Public API Entry Point

1.1 Call: fmt::format("{}", x)
include/fmt/format.h:4363-4366
template <typename... T>
FMT_NODISCARD FMT_INLINE auto format(format_string<T...> fmt, T&&... args)
    -> std::string {
  return vformat(fmt, fmt::make_format_args(args...));
}

This is the main entry point. It's a template that:

  • Takes a format_string (the compile-time checked format literal)
  • Takes variadic arguments args...
  • Calls make_format_args() to capture arguments
  • Passes both to vformat()

Step 2: Type Erasure via make_format_args

2.1 Function: fmt::make_format_args(x)
include/fmt/base.h:2016-2020
template <typename Context = format_context, typename... T>
constexpr FMT_ALWAYS_INLINE auto make_format_args(T&... args)
    -> detail::format_arg_store<Context, NUM_ARGS, 0, DESC> {
  return {{detail::make_arg<NUM_ARGS <= detail::max_packed_args, Context>(
      args)...}};
}

This creates a format_arg_store that stores the type-erased arguments.

  • NUM_ARGS = number of arguments (compile-time)
  • DESC = descriptor encoding argument types (packed into an unsigned long long)
  • Each arg is passed through make_arg()
2.2 Type Erasure: make_arg<PACKED, Context>(T& val)
include/fmt/base.h:1620-1661
// For packed args (NUM_ARGS <= max_packed_args)
template <bool PACKED, typename Context, typename T, FMT_ENABLE_IF(PACKED)>
FMT_CONSTEXPR auto make_arg(T& val) -> value<Context> {
  using arg_type = remove_cvref_t<decltype(arg_mapper<Context>().map(val))>;
  // ... compile-time checks for formattability ...
  return {arg_mapper<Context>().map(val)};
}

// For unpacked args (NUM_ARGS > max_packed_args)
template <typename Context, typename T>
FMT_CONSTEXPR auto make_arg(T& val) -> basic_format_arg<Context> {
  auto arg = basic_format_arg<Context>();
  arg.type_ = mapped_type_constant<T, Context>::value;
  arg.value_ = make_arg<true, Context>(val);
  return arg;
}

The key insights:

  • arg_mapper converts user types to fmt's internal representation (ints stay ints, strings become string_view, etc.)
  • For packed args (≤4 on 64-bit): type info goes into the descriptor, values into a union
  • For unpacked args: type + value stored together in basic_format_arg
  • Compile-time checks verify the type is formattable

template <typename Context> class value {
 public:
  union {
    monostate no_value;
    int int_value;
    unsigned uint_value;
    long long long_long_value;
    bool bool_value;
    char_type char_value;
    float float_value;
    double double_value;

struct format_arg_store {

Key Design Insights

  • Type Erasure via Descriptor: Small count of args (≤4) → types packed in a 64-bit descriptor. Larger counts → type stored with value. Saves binary size.
  • Compile-Time Checks: make_format_args() is template-instantiated per call site, enabling compile-time verification that arguments are formattable.
  • Visitor Pattern: visit() re-instantiates the erased type by using a switch on the type field. The visitor is then called with the recovered type.
  • Custom Types via Function Pointers: For user types, a function pointer to the instantiated formatter is stored. This avoids needing virtual functions.
  • Format Specs Parsed at Runtime: Width, precision, alignment are parsed from the format string by the format_handler and passed to the formatter.
  • Buffer Abstraction: All output goes to a buffer via an appender iterator. The buffer grows as needed, and is only converted to std::string at the end.

  case detail::type::double_type:
    return vis(value_.double_value);
  case detail::type::cstring_type:
    return vis(value_.string.data);

Step 6: Formatting with default_arg_formatter or arg_formatter

6.1 Without specs: default_arg_formatter<Char>
include/fmt/format.h:3718-3735
template <typename Char> struct default_arg_formatter {
  using iterator = basic_appender<Char>;
  using context = buffered_context<Char>;

  iterator out;
  basic_format_args<context> args;
  locale_ref loc;

  template <typename T> auto operator()(T value) -> iterator {
    return write<Char>(out, value);
  }
  auto operator()(typename basic_format_arg<context>::handle h) -> iterator {
    basic_format_parse_context<Char> parse_ctx({});
    context format_ctx(out, args, loc);
    h.format(parse_ctx, format_ctx);  // Calls user's formatter
    return format_ctx.out();
  }

  • For custom types: calls the stored format function pointer
6.2 With specs: arg_formatter<Char>
include/fmt/format.h:3737-3754
template <typename Char> struct arg_formatter {
  using iterator = basic_appender<Char>;
  using context = buffered_context<Char>;

  iterator out;
  const format_specs& specs;  // width, precision, alignment, etc.
  locale_ref locale;

  template <typename T>
  FMT_CONSTEXPR FMT_INLINE auto operator()(T value) -> iterator {
    return detail::write<Char>(out, value, specs, locale);
  }
  auto operator()(typename basic_format_arg<context>::handle) -> iterator {
    return out;  // Custom types handle specs internally

7.1 Function: detail::write<Char>(out, value, [specs, locale])
include/fmt/format.h:1923-1931, 2217-2236, 3661-3714

// For characters
template <typename Char, typename T,
          FMT_ENABLE_IF(std::is_same<T, Char>::value)>
FMT_CONSTEXPR auto write(OutputIt out, Char value, const format_specs& specs,
                         locale_ref loc = {}) -> OutputIt;

// For integral types (int, long, etc.)
template <typename Char, typename T,
          FMT_ENABLE_IF(is_integral<T>::value &&
                        !std::is_same<T, bool>::value)>
FMT_CONSTEXPR FMT_INLINE auto write(basic_appender<Char> out, T value,
                                    const format_specs& specs, locale_ref loc)
    -> basic_appender<Char> {
  if (specs.localized && write_loc(out, value, specs, loc)) return out;
  return write_int_noinline<Char>(out, make_write_int_arg(value, specs.sign),
                                    specs, loc);
}

// For strings
template <typename Char, typename OutputIt, typename T,
          FMT_ENABLE_IF(has_to_string_view<T>::value)>
FMT_CONSTEXPR auto write(OutputIt out, const T& value) -> OutputIt;

// For floating point
template <typename Char, typename T,
          FMT_ENABLE_IF(is_floating_point<T>::value)>
FMT_CONSTEXPR auto write(OutputIt out, T value, const format_specs& specs = {},
                         locale_ref = {}) -> OutputIt;

  • Takes the appropriate type (recovered from the visit dispatch)
  • Applies format specs (width, precision, alignment)
  • Writes the formatted result to the out iterator (the buffer)
7.2 For Custom Types: The handle.format() call
include/fmt/base.h:1747-1754
class handle {
 public:
  explicit handle(detail::custom_value<Context> custom) : custom_(custom) {}

  void format(typename Context::parse_context_type& parse_ctx,
              Context& ctx) const {
    custom_.format(custom_.value, parse_ctx, ctx);
  }

 private:
  detail::custom_value<Context> custom_;
};

// custom_value structure:
template <typename Context> struct custom_value {
  using parse_context = typename Context::parse_context_type;
  void* value;  // Pointer to the actual object
  void (*format)(void* arg, parse_context& parse_ctx, Context& ctx);
                // Function pointer to the formatter's format() method
};

For a custom type like struct MyType, when you provide fmt::formatter<MyType> specialization:

  • A pointer to the MyType object is stored in custom_.value
  • A function pointer to the formatter's format() method is stored
  • Later, when the argument is visited, this function is called
  • The function instantiates the formatter<MyType> and calls its parse()` and `format() methods
7.3 The formatter Template: What users specialize
include/fmt/base.h:1138-1144
template <typename T, typename Char = char, typename Enable = void>
struct formatter {
  // A deleted default constructor indicates a disabled formatter.
  formatter() = delete;
};

Users specialize this template. For example:

// User's custom formatter specialization
template <>
struct fmt::formatter<MyType> {
  auto parse(format_parse_context& ctx) {
    // Parse format specs from the format string
    return ctx.begin();
  }

  auto format(const MyType& obj, format_context& ctx) const {
    // Write the formatted output to ctx.out()
    return fmt::format_to(ctx.out(), "MyType(...)", obj.field);
  }
};

The fmt library calls these methods via the stored function pointer.

Step 8: Buffer to String Conversion

8.1 Converting Buffer to String: to_string(buffer)
include/fmt/format.h:4202-4207
template <typename Char, size_t SIZE>
FMT_NODISCARD auto to_string(const basic_memory_buffer<Char, SIZE>& buf)
    -> std::basic_string<Char> {
  auto size = buf.size();
  detail::assume(size < std::basic_string<Char>().max_size());
  return std::basic_string<Char>(buf.data(), size);
}

After vformat_to() finishes writing to the buffer:

  • All formatted output (literal text + formatted arguments) is in the buffer
  • to_string() creates a new std::string from the buffer's data
  • This string is returned to the caller

Complete Example Trace

For fmt::format("{}", 42):

1. format("{}", 42) → format_string<int>, args=(42) 2. make_format_args(42) → Creates format_arg_store: - args[0] = value{.int_value = 42} - desc_ encodes: type::int_type at position 0 3. format_arg_store → basic_format_args → Converts descriptor + values to queryable format_args 4. vformat(string_view("{}"), format_args) → Creates memory_buffer 5. vformat_to(buffer, "{}", format_args) → Parses "{}" → Calls args.get(0) → Returns format_arg{type_: int_type, value_: 42} → Calls arg.visit(default_arg_formatter{...}) → switch(int_type) → vis(42) → default_arg_formatter::operator()(42) → write<char>(out, 42) → Dispatches to integer write overload → Converts 42 to "42", appends to buffer 6. to_string(buffer) → Returns std::string("42")

Key Design Insights

  • Type Erasure via Descriptor: Small count of args (≤4) → types packed in a 64-bit descriptor. Larger counts → type stored with value. Saves binary size.
  • Compile-Time Checks: make_format_args() is template-instantiated per call site, enabling compile-time verification that arguments are formattable.
  • Visitor Pattern: visit() re-instantiates the erased type by using a switch on the type field. The visitor is then called with the recovered type.
  • Custom Types via Function Pointers: For user types, a function pointer to the instantiated formatter is stored. This avoids needing virtual functions.
  • Format Specs Parsed at Runtime: Width, precision, alignment are parsed from the format string by the format_handler and passed to the formatter.
  • Buffer Abstraction: All output goes to a buffer via an appender iterator. The buffer grows as needed, and is only converted to std::string at the end.

## What Happens When You Call `fmt::format("{}", x)`

### **High-Level Pipeline:**

```
fmt::format("{}", x)
    ↓
make_format_args(x)  [type-erasure]
    ↓
vformat()  [creates buffer]
    ↓
vformat_to()  [parses format string & visits args]
    ↓
formatter specializations  [writes each arg]
    ↓
to_string(buffer)  [returns std::string]
```

---

### **Key Stages:**

**1. Type Erasure via `make_format_args()` (base.h:2016-2020)**
- Takes each argument through `make_arg<T>()`
- `arg_mapper` converts the type (int stays int, strings become string_view, etc.)
- Creates a `format_arg_store` that stores:
  - **Type info** in a descriptor (packed into an `unsigned long long`)
  - **Values** in a union (`value<Context>`)
- For ≤4 args: types packed into descriptor bits; values stored separately
- For >4 args: type + value stored together as `basic_format_arg`

**2. Implicit Conversion to `format_args` (base.h:1879-1892)**
- `format_arg_store` converts to `basic_format_args`
- Stores descriptor + pointer to values/args
- This is the **type-erased view** passed to `vformat()`

**3. Buffer Creation and Formatting (`vformat`, format-inl.h:1431-1437)**
- Creates a `memory_buffer` (resizable byte buffer)
- Calls `detail::vformat_to()` to format into the buffer
- Converts buffer to `std::string` via `to_string()`

**4. Format String Parsing (`vformat_to`, format.h:4220-4286)**
- Parses the format string using `parse_format_string<>()`
- For each `{}` or `{:specs}` placeholder:
  - Fetches the argument via `args.get(id)`
  - Calls `arg.visit(formatter)`

**5. Type Re-instantiation via `visit()` (base.h:1778-1816)**
- **This is the magic!** The visit method:
  - Switches on the stored `type_` field
  - Extracts the correct value from the union
  - Calls the visitor function with the recovered type
  - Example: if `type_ == int_type`, extracts `value_.int_value` and calls `visitor(42)`

**6. Formatting with `default_arg_formatter` or `arg_formatter` (format.h:3718-3754)**
- `default_arg_formatter` (no specs): calls `write<Char>(out, value)`
- `arg_formatter` (with specs): calls `write<Char>(out, value, specs, locale)`
- For custom types: calls the stored formatter function pointer

**7. Type-Specific `write()` Dispatch (format.h:1923-1931, 2217-2236, etc.)**
- Many overloads of `write()` for each type (int, double, string, etc.)
- Each applies format specs and writes to the buffer via an `appender` iterator

**8. Custom Type Handling via `handle.format()`**
- User provides `fmt::formatter<MyType>` specialization
- `parse()` method parses format specs from the format string
- `format()` method writes the formatted output
- Accessed through the stored function pointer

**9. Final Conversion (format.h:4202-4207)**
- `to_string(buffer)` creates a `std::string` from the formatted buffer
- Returned to the caller

---

### **Key Files:**
- **Public API:** `include/fmt/format.h:4363-4366` (`format()` template)
- **Type erasure:** `include/fmt/base.h` (`make_format_args`, `basic_format_arg`, `basic_format_args`, `value<Context>`, `formatter<T>`)
- **Formatting:** `include/fmt/format.h:4220-4286` (`vformat_to()`)
- **Implementation:** `include/fmt/format-inl.h:1431-1437` (`vformat()`)
